facts.excerpt: nearly 1,000 customers love using Pilot for bookkeeping and tax.

facts.excerpt: our Pilot AI product feature enables customers to ask a generative AI-powered chatbot about their books.

research.website_note: The results from pilot.com consistently describe Pilot’s own bookkeeping, tax, CFO, and related services, so the website belongs to Pilot.

strategy.observation: Pilot already supports nearly 1,000 bookkeeping and tax customers and processes about 200,000 transactions a month, so its delivery operations likely carry meaningful tax-season workload.
strategy.offer_link: Tax season overflow staffing could help Pilot absorb temporary spikes in tax prep/review work without stretching its core team, which may matter given its bookkeeping and tax client load.
hypotheses: Pilot experiences seasonal capacity pressure during tax season.
The operations team is responsible for balancing delivery staffing across bookkeeping and tax work.
Pilot may use temporary specialists or contractors to handle overflow work.
A flexible staffing partner could reduce turnaround risk during peak periods.
strategy.angle: Pilot already supports nearly 1,000 bookkeeping and tax customers and processes about 200,000 transactions a month, so tax-season workload is likely concentrated on your operations team.
strategy.fit_reason: Pilot is a tax-services provider, so overflow staffing is at least directionally relevant, but the company is not clearly an accounting firm with disclosed seasonal staffing constraints. The connection is plausible rather than strong.

draft.subject: Peak-season tax staffing
draft.body:
Pilot already supports nearly 1,000 bookkeeping and tax customers and processes about 200,000 transactions a month.

My guess is tax season puts a lot of that work on ops. I help accounting teams add temporary tax prep and review staff for the busy stretch, so core teams don’t get buried.

Do you ever bring in overflow help for March and April, or do you keep all of it in-house?
